El consejo de construir un lenguaje pequ: The advice to build a small language in order to learn is old and has been given in several forms. Niklaus Wirth designed Pascal in 1970 explicitly for teaching, and its compiler fitted on a machine of the period; then he made one language after another, each smaller than the last, with the idea that simplicity was the goal and not the starting point. His most quoted sentence sums up the whole block better than any summary: “making something simple is hard, and making it complicated is easy”. Pizca has seven words for that reason, and everything built here fits in three files that can be read at a sitting.

After writing an analyser, any compiler's error messages stop being a wall and read as what they are; after writing a compiler, it is much harder to believe that a program does something that cannot be explained.
